newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut asks U.S. to evacuate Lebanese from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Beirut asks U.S. to evacuate Lebanese from Zaire.

text.p: Lebanon has asked the United States to help evacuate Lebanese residents from Zaire, a Lebanese official said on Tuesday.

Lebanon had asked its charge d'affaires in Zaire to "contact the U.S. ambassador in Kinshasa and cooperate with him to evacuate the Lebanese residents there," Foreign Ministry Director-General Zafer al-Hassan told reporters after meeting U.S. diplomat Ronald Schlicher in Beirut.
Schlicher said the United States had received the Lebanese request.

"At this point there has been no decision to evacuate American citizens from Zaire...If there is a decision to evacuate Americans the American ambassador in Kinshasa will also have the authority to authorise the evacuation of other third country nationals," he said.
There are 5,000 registered Lebanese nationals in Zaire, where rebels seeking to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko have seized nearly half the Central African country.
Beirut newspapers recently reported that Zairean rebels took 65 Lebanese nationals hostage, demanding a ransom of nearly $1 million. Most of the Lebanese in Zaire are traders.
